claims.text: The initial sub-10 nm equiatomic Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles are metastable solid solutions with high configurational entropy.
The proposed intervention heats the nanoparticles under vacuum from 300 K to 1000 K.
In sub-10 nm Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles, surface-energy minimization and size-dependent vacancy supersaturation dominate over the bulk sluggish-diffusion effect.
Au and Cu have lower surface energies than Co, Ni, and Pt and therefore migrate to the nanoparticle surface.
Surface segregation enriches Co, Ni, and Pt in the particle core.
The high curvature of sub-10 nm particles lowers the activation barrier for surface atomic diffusion relative to bulk lattice diffusion.
Surface diffusion coefficients are orders of magnitude higher than bulk diffusion coefficients.
The surface-energy driving force for structural evolution scales inversely with particle radius.
Surface-energy-driven Ostwald ripening dissolves the smallest particles, particularly those below 5 nm.
Material from dissolving small particles causes the remaining particles to grow.
Heating causes initially spherical particles to become faceted as surface-energy anisotropy overtakes entropic stabilization.
Heating produces Au/Cu-rich shells and Co/Ni/Pt-rich cores or complete elemental segregation.
Co-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ni high-entropy alloys exhibit sluggish diffusion associated with elevated diffusion activation energies.
Lattice distortion is responsible for sluggish diffusion in bulk high-entropy alloys.
Bulk-HEA behavior provides a baseline in which sluggish diffusion and entropy maintain a single-phase solid solution and prevent phase separation through 1000 K.
The surface-diffusion-dominated regime applies below 10 nm, where the surface-to-volume ratio exceeds 20%.
Above 50 nm, bulk lattice diffusion and configurational entropy dominate over the proposed surface mechanism.
Bulk TiCoCrFeMn exhibits structural stability during prolonged annealing at 1000 degrees Celsius.
The segregation sequence in Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt depends on its element-specific surface energies and mixing enthalpies.
